title: Erdős Problem 173: monochromatic triangles in two-colorings of the plane
summary: A Lean proof that in every two-coloring of the plane any three distinct points that are not the vertices of an equilateral triangle, collinear points included, have a monochromatic congruent copy and at most one equilateral side length is missed, so at most one triangle up to congruence, degenerate or not, has no monochromatic copy. Alternating strips show that one equilateral triangle can be missed. This answers Erdős Problem 173 as Bloom states it and settles the conjecture of Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer and Straus that every non-equilateral triangle has a monochromatic…

review.reason: Lean proof addressing an Erdős problem on monochromatic triangles in plane colorings.
